newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreign demand pushes Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Foreign demand pushes Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index sustained its upward movement on Monday pushed by foreign demand on key shares in the market.
The index went up 7.50 points to stand at 3063.90. Turnover was posted at 23.384 million shillings traded on 551,109 shares from 153.411 million shillings traded on 3,484,582 shares on Friday.
Brokers and bourse officials said foreign investors were the highlight of the day, accounting for about 40 percent of the activity in the market.
They bought 57,000 shares of Kenya Breweries at 50 from 51.50 and 140,000 shares of Uchumi Supermarket at 44.75 from 43.50.
Kenya Commercial Bank traded at 69 from 66 on the normal board -- a premium of 19 from the last offer price of 50. The offer for sale closed on October 15.
In the Agriculturals, only Rea Vipingo REAV.NR. traded at 10.30 from 10.50. Brokers said there were bids for Kakuzi and George Williamson Kenya mainly from foreign investors.

There was an air of excitement as the first corporate bonds were traded on the secondary market today, (Monday). These were issued by the East African Development Bank and were pegged to Monday's interest rate on the 91-day category of treasury bills -- 21.36 percent.
Some brokers said that despite the upward movement of the index in the last two weeks, local investors had not regained their confidence in the market.
"In fact if you split the market into two, you'll find the locals are on the selling side, while the foreign institutional investors are on the buying side," one broker said.
